stem: A child is reviewed after an episode of acute otitis media and still has middle ear fluid but no signs or symptoms of inflammation; what is the best term for this finding?
explanation: Otitis media with effusion is the correct term for middle ear fluid without signs or symptoms of inflammation.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because acute otitis media involves acute inflammation, pain or fever, not just persistent fluid after infection.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because otitis media with effusion is middle ear fluid without signs or symptoms of inflammation, often following an episode of acute otitis media.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because mastoiditis is a more severe complication with mastoid inflammation, not uncomplicated middle ear effusion.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because otitis media with effusion does not routinely require antibiotics.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because chronic suppurative otitis media involves persistent ear discharge through a perforated tympanic membrane, not a non-inflamed effusion.
